The terminal a frame is drawn on travels with the frame (rich-animation-27tq.lfw)

Every colour effect was handed the terminal when it was built, so two effects
in one frame could name different terminals, and a user container's caller had
to carry it down to the leaves. It is now `RenderOptions.terminal`, beside
`colorSystem`: a program names it once on its Console, App or renderToString,
and `Recolored.moved` is the one read of it. ProgressBar reads it too, where it
had hard-coded the depth's assumed terminal.

`theme` comes off `EffectedOptions`, `throughColors` and `Between`.
`Drawn.theme` becomes `Drawn.terminal`, since `RenderOptions.theme` already
means the style names. Each is a compile error for a caller, not a silent
change. `drawnOf` keeps its argument: it measures segments the caller holds and
builds no effect.

Each peer, pinned and on disk, is the lowest version its range admits (rich-unfiled-791c.25dh) (#526)

* Each optional peer on disk is the lowest version its range admits (rich-unfiled-791c.25dh)

Nothing tied the peer ranges to what src/ compiles against: on
rich-animation-27tq.0gd src/ imported a 0.11.0 export under a ^0.10.0 range and
only a code review saw it. With the peers held at their floors, lint is the
compile at the floor and the suite runs there too, so the gate needs no registry,
temp tree or second tsc. It reads the version on disk rather than the lockfile,
because that incident was a --no-save tarball the lockfile never saw.

* The manifest pins each peer at its floor, and the gate covers every peer (rich-unfiled-791c.25dh)

devDependencies held caret ranges that admitted the very trees the gate
refuses, so a routine npm update went red on a change nobody meant as a floor
decision. Exact pins leave only a deliberate edit able to move the tree.

The gate now reads every peer, not only optional ones; a dropped
peerDependenciesMeta row would have taken a peer out of it silently. A
non-semver range is refused with the peer's name, versions compare through
semver, and the failure message no longer offers raising the range to a version
the registry may not have.

* A peer's devDependencies pin is the floor too, and the gate checks it (rich-unfiled-791c.25dh)

npm writes a caret back on any plain install -D, so the pin the last commit
added could not be assumed, and a file: spec holding the right version would
have passed while the range named nothing the registry serves. The failure
message names no version to install, since a range's floor may be unpublished.

* The gate claims nothing about the registry, and says how to answer a stale install (rich-unfiled-791c.25dh)

An exact pin does not stop a lockfile resolving to a tarball, so the header stops
saying an npm ci tree proves a floor is published and names that as a blind spot.
The message now separates the stale install from the meant bump, and says the
range is what a bump has to move.
